intro:
Transylvania's seat 4 (far right): drawn facing the viewer's right and MIRRORED by the game to face the table's centre. Built the way Van Helsing is (`art-tools/pose_rig.py`), in the GOTHIC style (the owner, after the flat sheet came out childish: 'split the difference' with the dark table mock-ups; the design doc's tone is 'dark and gothic with deliberate bright spots'). His approved character sheet is the style reference for the rest of the table.

His look, from his character file and Irving: huge, cloaked and square-shouldered, stopping abruptly at the collar; the missing head is the strongest shape at the table. A Hessian trooper's coat (blue with red facings) under a heavy riding cloak, gauntlets, a cavalry sword. On his collar sits a carved pumpkin with a plain candle inside, and its LIGHT is the tell surface: brighter, guttering. He has no face, so the face sheet is the pumpkin in its states of light.

Ruled out (his character file): Disney's 1949 cartoon and Burton's 1999 film: no flaming jack-o'-lantern with a leering grin, no cackle, no filed teeth, no actor's head, no tree of the dead. The candle is our addition, not Irving's, and stays a plain candle. Layout from Lancelot's character sheet, mood from `art-tools/style/gothic_mood.png`.

Tags (MOTION-SPEC.md): his three tells, each beside the idle it hides among: the candle burning brighter (strong) beside settling the pumpkin on his collar (light and pumpkin both times); the flame guttering (tilted) beside a cold smell of leaves drifting from him (a faint drift of dead leaves); drumming a gauntlet on the table (weak) beside his sword rattling in its scabbard (a hand moving at the table). 'Turns his whole body to look at you' is C4.

The owner's tweaks to the approved sheet: battered plate armour and a ragged cloak with brass skull bosses in place of the Hessian coat (a revenant, not a trooper on parade), and a classic carved jack-o'-lantern face with jagged teeth, angry rather than laughing. The candle still never becomes fire pouring out of the head (that, and a laughing face, stay Disney's).

howto: One fresh ChatGPT chat for all six. The first prompt attaches TWO images, in this order: Lancelot's character sheet (`art-tools/lancelot_parts/sources/lancelot_sheet.png`) for the layout, then the owner's gothic table mock-up (`art-tools/style/gothic_mood.png`) for the MOOD only (the prompt forbids its Universal-style monster, its pumpkin and its interface). From the second prompt on, attach the Horseman's own character sheet (`sources/headless_horseman_sheet.png`, the owner's tweaked version: plate armour, skull bosses, a jagged-toothed carving) and his pose sheet A once it exists, and nothing else: his sheet is the style reference. The first, flat-cartoon sheet is kept in `sources/rejected/` (the owner: 'childish').
character:
Character sheet for 2D animation rigging: the Headless Horseman, of Washington Irving's The Legend of Sleepy Hollow (1820): the ghost of a Hessian trooper whose head was carried away by a cannonball. Copy ONLY the LAYOUT of the FIRST attached sheet (what goes where): take NOTHING of its character. No plate armour, no striped surcoat, no long hair. Take the MOOD from the SECOND attached image, as the STYLE rule at the end says.

The Headless Horseman: a HUGE, square-shouldered soldier with NO HEAD: his body stops abruptly at a high black stock and coat collar. A dark blue Hessian soldier's coat of 1776 with red facings and brass buttons, a buff waistcoat, a heavy black riding cloak thrown over his broad shoulders, big brown leather gauntlets; the brass hilt of a cavalry sword rises beside his left hip. On his collar, where his head should be, sits a heavy, lopsided old pumpkin, deep orange going brown, its skin scarred and its stalk dried black, carved by a knife with a GRIM face: two narrow, slanted, angular eye holes and a long, jagged, downturned slit of a mouth, NOT smiling, NOT grinning; a plain candle burning inside, its hard orange light spilling out of the holes and lighting the top of his collar from below. No flames come out of it. The missing head is his strongest shape: the empty space above the collar must read at a tiny size. Huge, silent, cold and patient, a revenant soldier: dread, not comedy. NO flames pouring out of the pumpkin, NO laughing or grinning face, NO cackling, NO horse, nothing from Disney's 1949 cartoon or any film.

Pure white background (#FFFFFF). Every piece separate, with a closed dark outline and a wide gap all round it; nothing touches or overlaps. No text, no labels, no frames, no cast shadows.

The angle: a gentle three-quarter view, turned about 25 degrees from front-on, facing the viewer's right. The pumpkin's face and both shoulders clearly visible. NOT profile.

Draw, all facing the viewer's right, at the same size:
- The pumpkin on the collar, with the stock and the top of the coat, four times: candle steady; candle burning BRIGHT, a strong warm glow round the holes; flame guttering, the light dim and flickering; candle out, the holes dark
- The headless torso in the coat, cloak and waistcoat, the stock and collar at the top with NOTHING above it: cut off straight below the waist, the upper arms down to the elbows; NO forearms, NO hands
- Two forearms in the coat sleeves with brown gauntlets, lying on a table, pointing toward its centre, open at the elbow end
- On their own: the carved pumpkin, candle lit; the brass sword hilt and the top of its scabbard
- Four seated reference poses, waist up behind the curved edge of a round green poker table, forearms resting on its edge, gauntlets apart: candle steady; candle burning bright; the fingers of his right gauntlet drumming on the felt; flame guttering

A: At rest: both forearms lying along the table's edge, his steel gauntlets resting on the felt in front of him, a hand's width apart, relaxed and NOT touching, NOT laced, NOT overlapping; the pumpkin square on his collar, candle steady
Peeking at his cards: his right gauntlet cupped over two cards on the felt, thumb lifting the near corner, the pumpkin tipped down toward them
Checking: one finger of his right gauntlet tapping the felt
Calling: his right gauntlet sliding a short stack of chips forward
Betting: his right gauntlet pushing a stack of chips well forward
Folding: his right gauntlet flicking two cards away face down
B: All in: both gauntlets pushing his whole stack of chips forward, the pumpkin's light bright
Showing: his right gauntlet turning two cards face up; the card faces are BLANK white, no ranks, no suits
Collecting the pot: both forearms out on the felt, drawing a pile of chips in
The candle in his pumpkin burning BRIGHTER: a strong warm glow round the eye holes and mouth slit and a soft halo of light round the whole pumpkin; the rest of him perfectly still, arms as at rest
Settling the pumpkin on his collar: both gauntlets lifted to the pumpkin, holding it at the sides, straightening it on his collar, candle steady
Drumming a gauntlet on the table: the fingers of his right gauntlet raised and drumming on the felt, two short motion lines beside them; left arm as at rest
C: His sword rattling in its scabbard: his left gauntlet resting on a brass sword hilt that rises just above the table's edge at his left side, two short rattle lines beside the hilt; right arm as at rest
The flame in his pumpkin GUTTERING: the light inside dim and uneven, the eye holes nearly dark, a thin curl of smoke rising from the top of the pumpkin; arms as at rest
A smell of cold leaves drifting from him: a few brown dead leaves and a faint pale wisp drifting up and away from his cloak; arms as at rest, candle steady
Turning his whole body toward the viewer, shoulders squared to the viewer, the pumpkin facing the viewer; arms as at rest
Drawing his black cloak about his shoulders with his right gauntlet
Sitting very still, the pumpkin tilted a little toward the middle of the table (the right of the picture), as if listening; arms as at rest
D: Talking: his right gauntlet raised a little, palm open, the pumpkin's light pulsing a little brighter at the mouth slit
Facing a big bet: leaning back, both gauntlets flat on the felt, the pumpkin's light low and steady
Lost a pot: his shoulders slumped, the pumpkin tipped forward, its light dimmed; arms as at rest
Won a pot: his right gauntlet drawing a few chips toward him, the pumpkin's light bright
Down to two players: leaning in on both forearms, the pumpkin lowered toward the viewer, its light bright
Knocked out: rising from his seat, the pumpkin lifted off his collar and tucked under his left arm, candle out, turning away toward the left of the picture

face:
Character sheet for 2D animation rigging: the Headless Horseman's pumpkin, exactly matching the attached sheets' style, colours and line weight. He has NO head and NO face: the pumpkin on his collar is his face, and its candlelight is how he shows anything.

Every piece is drawn at EXACTLY the angle and size of the pumpkin in the at-rest pose (three-quarter, facing the viewer's right), so each one can be laid over it. Draw the pumpkin once, top left, sitting on the high riveted collar, as the reference, candle steady. Then every piece separate, with a closed dark outline and a wide gap all round it; nothing touches. Pure white background (#FFFFFF). No text, no labels. The carved face is ALWAYS the same one as on the attached character sheet: two angry, slanted, angular eyes and a jagged-toothed mouth, the same scars. Only the light changes.

- The pumpkin alone, its candle at different strengths, one piece each: steady; brighter; very bright, with a warm halo; dim; guttering, uneven light, a thin curl of smoke; out, the holes dark
- The glow at the mouth slit only, for speech, three pieces: a little brighter; brighter; brightest
- The pumpkin turned toward the viewer, nearly front-on, candle steady
style: STYLE, the most important rule: a GOTHIC GRAPHIC-NOVEL style for a grown-up card game, halfway between a bright cartoon and a dark painted illustration. Take ONLY the mood and rendering of the SECOND attached image: its deep shadows, its candle and moonlight, its rich, muted colour and its sense of menace. Take NOTHING else from it: none of its characters, NOT its pumpkin, NOT its green-skinned monster, none of its interface, cards or chips. Keep what the game needs: a bold dark outline round every shape, big clear readable shapes, a silhouette that reads at a tiny size. Add what makes it grown-up: adult, realistic proportions (never a big head, never chibi, never cute); shading in three or four tones with deep, dramatic shadows and a warm rim light from candlelight; rich but MUTED colour (deep navy, oxblood red, tarnished brass, aged leather), nothing candy-bright; cloth with real weight and heavy folds; leather and metal with worn edges and soft highlights, a little texture in the shadows only. Serious, cold and imposing. NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute, NOT toy-like, NOT round and bouncy, NOT photoreal, NOT muddy or murky.
style_short: Keep the gothic graphic-novel style of the attached character sheet: bold dark outlines, adult proportions, deep three- or four-tone shading, a warm candlelit rim light, rich muted colour, worn leather and metal; serious and imposing, NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute.
